enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction. Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVBMESIE003YQ68** – AI should focus fire on the boss (open)
- **AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5** – PlayScene mini-boss integration (completed)

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever
   scene-specific scenario parameters it needs (enemy roster, formation, level,
   toggles) through the capture scene config, so any gym can be driven from
   `examples/scenes.json` and recorded. Extend the config validation and the
   `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / parameterised-scene contracts accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`)
      with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit
      target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live
      `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then
      snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails
      on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` /
      `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in
      `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity
      test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's
      block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.
- [ ] AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once**
      repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site
      (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it;
      the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.
- [ ] AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene
      under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the
      level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it
      inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges —
      the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in
      this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those
      already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.
- [ ] AC6 — Every gym applies the shared scripted-scene `setup` seam and exposes
      its scenario parameters through the capture scene config, so any gym can
      be launched and recorded from `examples/scenes.json`; the scene-config
      validator rejects unsupported/parameterised targets with a clear error, and
      the `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract and its pinning test are
      updated.
- [ ] AC7 — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (and `AGENTS.md`
      § Game Architecture Conventions where the rule text changes) explain the
      shared spawn seam and point at the parity matrix; the docs guard test still
      passes.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
      including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site
      entries (including the scripted-scene/gym capture documentation).
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No balance changes. Behavioural differences introduced by this item must be a
  *fix toward* the game's behaviour, except where the producer explicitly asks
  for a new gym capability (scripted-scene setup, AC6).
- Must not "fix" documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE
  practice targets, flat formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD); each must keep
  its documented reason.
- Must not regress the automation that consumes the gyms: the capture CLI and
  `sceneSetup` appliers, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, and the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract.
- Scope is deliberately broad (producer direction: sweep and fix all in this
  item). If the sweep uncovers a divergence that cannot be fixed without a
  separate design decision, record it as a blocker with evidence on this item
  rather than silently expanding the design.
- The item is expected to be decomposed into child items at the plan stage
  (shared seam, spawn-parity fixes, gym sweep, scripted-scene adoption, docs);
  the ACs above are the whole-item contract.
- The reported symptom must be reproducible before the fix and demonstrably
  fixed after it (red-before / green-after per repo convention).
- Implementation runs in the item's own worktree per `AGENTS.md`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` — **new** shared destination-resolver seam
  (orbital slot / offset fallback / autonomous exemption / live-slot tracking).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — consume the shared seam from `_spawnEnemy`;
  keep march state as the single source for block anchoring.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — replace its inline resolver.

# Scripted scenes for video (excitement-curve scene arc)

**Headline:** Author the example scripted-video scene list — a seven-scene excitement-curve arc (maxed-out opener → humble beginnings → escalating encounters → mini-boss → reprise → final boss) rendered by `npm run capture:scenes` — backed by a small dev-gated setup extension so weapon levels 2–5, the Hull Full reward, and the mini-boss/boss deaths are deterministic on camera, replacing `examples/scenes.json` and recorded once end-to-end.

## Problem statement

The capture pipeline (`npm run capture:scenes -- --config scenes.json`) can already compile any scene list into one video with 0.25 s cross-fades, and the current example (`examples/scenes.json`) demonstrates the schema with a generic showcase. What is missing is **the actual example video content for a scripted, narrative arc**: a scene list whose content deliberately rises in excitement — from a visually loaded opening, through an under-powered early scene, to escalating enemy pressure and two boss pay-offs, each beat ending on a definite on-camera outcome. The scene-capture `setup` seam cannot yet express the specific beats the arc demands: weapons starting above level 1, a guaranteed Hull Full reward, and a mini-boss/boss that dies inside the capture window.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want a ready-to-run example scene config for the scripted video that follows the agreed excitement curve — opening on a fully upgraded, heavily-outfought spectacle, then dropping to a humble early scene and building back up through escalating encounters to a mini-boss and the main boss — so a recorded showcase video tells a satisfying arc instead of a flat sequence, and each scene's ending (Hull Full reward, mini-boss death, boss death) lands on camera.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants the example scripted video to demonstrate the game's range (from bare-cannon play to a fully-upgraded arsenal) in one ~60–75 s showcase cut, with deterministic outcomes so the recording reproduces the intended arc.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the showcase: they should read a clear difficulty/excitement curve and understand the game's progression fantasy (starting weak, ending gloriously overpowered).

**Example user stories:**
- As the maintainer, I can run one command against the shipped example config and get the compiled arc video, so my demo footage follows the designed curve rather than a flat generic sequence.
- As the maintainer, I can tweak a number in the config (a weapon level, an enemy count, a seed) and re-record, trusting the rest of the arc and the on-camera endings to stay in place.
- As a viewer, I see each scene's payoff (Hull Full, mini-boss death, boss death) actually happen on screen, so the video reads as scripted rather than accidental.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — The seven-scene arc is authored as the example config.** `examples/scenes.json` is replaced by the excitement-curve arc in the exact beat order: (1) **Opening spectacle** — many enemies, lots of minerals and upgrades, all six upgrade slots filled with weapons at levels 2–5; (2) **Humble origins** — default weapon only, the wormhole spawns a few weak enemies, many asteroids to destroy and collect, ending with the player receiving the **Hull Full** reward; (3) **First steps up** — about 2× the enemies of scene 2, 3 weapon slots filled at level 1; (4) **Escalation** — 2× the enemies of scene 3, 5 slots filled at levels 1–2; (5) **Mini-boss** — a reasonable escort of enemies, all slots filled at levels 1–3, ending with the **mini-boss death**; (6) **Reprise** — similar pressure to scene 4, different enemies, more (stronger) player weapons; (7) **Main boss** — a heavy loadout, ending with the **boss death**. Each entry carries `target`, `playMs`, `captureMs`, `label` and the `setup` that realises its beat; the file passes the existing pre-boot scene-config validation unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — Deterministic arc beats via a small dev-gated setup extension.** The scene `setup` seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` → gyms) gains, with validated/normalised support in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (+ `.d.mts` types and error codes): (a) `player.weaponLevels` — per-weapon permanent levels 2–5 (existing `player.weapons` stays the level-1 grant path); (b) `setup.bossHitsRemaining` — the boss gyms (`GymBoss`, `GymMiniBoss`) spawn their entity with that many hits left (its `initialHp`), precedent `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario(bossHitsRemaining)` and the gyms' on-screen DAMAGE seams; (c) `setup.mineralReward` — the hold-full choice in the level gyms resolves to that reward id, so scene 2's Hull Full pay-off is deterministic. Each new field is validated, normalised and documented alongside the existing ones. The extension is dev-gated/inert for production: `npm run check-bundle` stays green and the gym↔game parity suite (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) stays green; no shipped-game gameplay behaviour changes.
- [ ] **AC3 — The recorded video verifies the arc and endings.** One end-to-end run — `npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json` — produces a single playable WebM (git-ignored `capture-output/…` or explicit `--output`), with the expected scene count, all fade probes passing (250 ms fades verified as dark), and the three scripted pay-offs (Hull Full resolution, mini-boss death, boss death) visible in their scenes' windows. Scene count/timings reported in the `--json` payload; the ~60–75 s target is the baseline (longer windows are acceptable where a beat needs them).
- [ ] **AC4 — The arc is seeded and reproducible.** Every setup-bearing scene carries a stable `seed`; re-running the config reproduces the same loadouts and (at the content level — minerals, drops, asteroid plan) the same playfield. The seeds are pinned by the hermetic tests so an author editing the file cannot silently lose determinism.
- [ ] **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Hermetic tests (extending `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`) cover: parse/validate/normalise/idempotence of the new setup fields, the exact scene-table assertions for the seven beats (targets, loadouts, slot counts, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`, seeds), applier tests in `sceneSetup.test.ts` for weapon levels / forced reward, and updated `examples/scenes.json` pins in `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` and `capture-scenes.test.ts` (both presently assert the *old* example's `GymFodderEnemies`/`PlayScene` entries — these expectations are updated to the new arc while keeping their validating intent). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the new setup fields (`player.weaponLevels`, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`), the two-way doc↔schema parity test is updated for them, and the example config is referenced; the README's existing `capture:scenes`/`scenes.json` cross-links remain accurate; code comments updated. (CHANGELOG.md is managed by the ship release pipeline and is excluded.)

## Constraints

- **Dev-gated only.** All scene-config content and the new setup fields are capture/dev tooling: no change to the shipped gameplay bundle (`npm run check-bundle` must stay green) and no new gameplay behaviour in `PlayScene`. The capture director and setups already exist only in dev builds; boss/mini-boss hit-preview is an explicit dev/capture-facing seam (as today's DAMAGE buttons in the gyms already are).
- **Gym↔game parity, no forked gameplay.** The loadout/power-up/seed mapping continues through the one shared `applySceneSetup` applier; gyms never copy game behaviour. The new fields only *configure* state the game already has (permanent weapon grants, `initialHp`, the hold-full choice strategy).
- **Schema single-source.** New setup fields are validated in the pure `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` module, typed in `capture-scenes.d.mts`, and pinned by tests + the docs parity test — one source of truth, no drift.
- **Deterministic where promised.** The three scripted pay-offs and the loadout/level progression are deterministic requirements; everything else (asteroid density, exact drop cadence) is seed-driven best effort documented as such.
- **UK English** in all written output and documentation. Keep changes surgical; report (do not delete) dead code.

## Existing state (verified 2026-10-27 against HEAD)

- Multi-scene capture ships and is documented: `npm run capture:scenes -- --config scenes.json` parses/validates the scene list before any browser boots, drives one continuous `MediaRecorder` across all scenes via the dev-gated in-page director (`window.__aiHellCaptureDirector`), and inserts 250 ms fade-to/from-black between scenes (`SCENE_FADE_MS`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`).
- `examples/scenes.json` is the generic showcase example: `GymPlayer`/`GymWeapons`/`GymPowerUpsCombat`, a `PlayScene` generated-level entry, one `GymLevel` setup, one `GymFodderEnemies` setup, and `GymBoss` — pinned by `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` and `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`.
- The scene `setup` seam (AH-0MVNW8VNN004FFK1) supports `level.waves[].groups[]` (enemyKey/formation/count/spacing), `startWave`, `player.weapons` (permanent, each granted **level 1**), `powerUps` (arbitrary levels), and `seed`. It is applied through the shared `applySceneSetup` so every gym (incl. `GymLevel`, `GymMiniBoss`, `GymBoss` via `GymFormationScene.init/create`) maps a setup to play state identically.
- `GymLevel` plays like the game: wormhole wave spawns, the shared asteroid hazard, the real mineral/drop supply layer, and the 30 s wave window — so authored levels reproduce game behaviour. A full mineral hold resolves automatically to one random reward in gyms (no modal, keeps the bot playing) — the seam a forced Hull Full reward hooks into.
- The good-boss/death precedent exists dev-gated in `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario(hitsRemaining)` (falls straight into the final boss phase with N hits left; `?scenario=boss&bossHits=N`). Boss phases are 50 hits each (200 total for the main boss); the mini-boss is 5 per phase × 3.
- Gym scene windows are recorded with **no player input**: the ship auto-fires from its spawn and does not move during a scene. Scene design must therefore bring the action to the ship (formation drift, wormhole/asteroid hazards, `mineral_scoop`/`magnet` pulling minerals and drops onto the ship) for the beats that read as "playing".

## Desired change

1. **Replace `examples/scenes.json`** with the seven-scene excitement-curve arc described in AC1, with per-scene setups (levels/waves/loadouts), seeds and labels, keeping the file schema-valid and pre-boot-valid.
2. **Extend the setup seam (dev-gated)** in `sceneSetup.ts` + `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (+ types/tests/docs): `player.weaponLevels` (permanent weapon levels 2–5), `bossHitsRemaining` for the boss gyms → `initialHp`, and `mineralReward` (forced hold-full reward id). Validation, normalisation, error codes, type declarations and doc parity for each new field.
3. **Wire the boss gyms** (`GymMiniBoss`, `GymBoss`) to consume `bossHitsRemaining` from the setup so the mini-boss/boss spawn close to death and die during the capture window; wire the level gyms' `_resolveMineralHold` to the forced reward.
4. **Author the arc content** so each beat's on-camera outcome lands inside its window, using the seeded supply (magnet/mineral-scoop pull, asteroid plan, drop cadence) to keep the footage lively with the auto-firing ship.
5. **Verify**: hermetic tests for the new fields and the scene table; update the two example-pinning doc tests; update `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`; run `npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json` once and confirm the recorded video (fades + pay-offs + `--json` scene report).

## Verification commands

```bash
# hermetic: the config parses/validates and the arc's scene table holds
npx vitest run scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts \
  src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts

# production bundle stays clean (dev-gated extension only)
npm run check-bundle

# record the arc once (writes capture-output/scenes-<timestamp>.webm)
npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json

# inspect the per-scene timings / seeds / level report
npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json --json
```

## Key Files (predicted)

- `examples/scenes.json` — **replaced** with the seven-scene excitement-curve arc (the deliverable content).
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` + `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` — new setup fields (`player.weaponLevels`, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`) parsed/validated/normalised; new error codes; type declarations.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` — hermetic tests for the new fields + the example scene-table assertions + idempotence.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — `applySceneSetup` extended: weapon-level grants (n permanent equips), forced mineral reward; `SceneSetupState` types.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — consume `bossHitsRemaining` (spawn `initialHp`), apply forced reward.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — `_resolveMineralHold` honours the setup-chosen reward id.
- `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` — update the `examples/scenes.json` pins and document the new field parity.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document the new setup fields and the excitement-curve example.
- `README.md` — keep `capture:scenes`/`scenes.json` cross-links accurate (update if the example description changes).
- `capture-output/scenes-<timestamp>.webm` (git-ignored) — the one recorded verification video (or an explicit `--output` path).

## Related work

- `AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC` — Scripted Gameplay Videos (parent epic, completed): multi-scene capture, fades, single WebM.
- `AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX` — generated-level (`PlayScene`) scenes in the sequence (completed): the level/`minWaves`/`maxCaptureMs` fields this config can reuse.
- `AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J` — multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM (completed).
- `AH-0MVNW90FB003H3KM` — determinism seed for scene setups (completed): the `seed` contract this arc relies on.
- `AH-0MVNW8VNN004FFK1` — shared scene-setup applier (completed): the seam this item extends.
- `AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44` — `boss` / `boss-four-hits` dev scenarios → `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario` (completed): the hits-remaining precedent.
- **Related work (automated report)**: see the appended report — `AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX`, `AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC`, `AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J`, plus repository matches in `README.md`, the Game Design Document and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — pay-offs drift out of window.** Player hits-per-second and seeded drop timing are not fully deterministic frame-to-frame, so even with `bossHitsRemaining`/`mineralReward` the death/Hull-Full moment could land a fraction outside the capture window. **Mitigation:** author windows with margin (windows that extend past the planned pay-off), use `bossHitsRemaining` small enough for the auto-fire to finish inside the window, verify on the recorded footage, and adjust windows/seeds at implementation time.
- **Risk — recording realism (stationary ship).** Gym scenes are captured with the auto-firing ship fixed at its spawn (no input/bot in the scene driver); footage could look static, harming the "destroy and collect" beat. **Mitigation:** design each scene so its action converges on the ship (wormhole spawns, asteroid hazard, magnet/mineral-scoop pull, formation drift); asteroids and enemies already drift toward the ship. **Scope-creep guardrail:** if hand-authored footage still reads too static, the fix is a *separate* driver-side per-scene input-plan item (scripts/ only), tracked as a follow-up work item — not in this item's scope.
- **Risk — example-pinning tests break.** Replacing the example contents breaks `multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` / `capture-scenes.test.ts` expectations (`GymFodderEnemies`/`PlayScene` entries, `seed 42`). **Mitigation:** update these assertions in the same change (AC5) and call it out in the commit.
- **Risk — scope creep into driver or game behaviour.** Adding bot/input plans or shipped-game features would balloon this item. **Mitigation:** the new seam is config/setup-only and dev-gated; anything else is a separate work item.
- **Assumption — "Hull Full reward" = the hold-full (mineral upgrade) reward.** The description's "player getting a Hull Full reward" is read as the hold-fills upgrade resolution, made deterministic via the forced `mineralReward` (the Mystery UFO *permanent grant* is a different mechanic and is not required). If the operator meant something else, that is a one-line clarification, noted in the Appendix.
- **Assumption — 2×/4× enemy references are authored base counts.** "About 2×" scenes 3–4 are authored relative to scene 2's base counts; the shared `applyEnemyCountScaling` may additionally scale by the level, so the brief pins scene *relative* would-be counts and the tests assert the authored groups.
- **Assumption — asteroid density is seed/best-effort.** The scheduled asteroid hazard is not setup-configurable; scenes rely on the seeded plan and window length. Recorded footage is the arbiter.
- **Assumption — "six slots of level 2–5 weapons" means six permanent weapon-drop grants.** The six upgrade slots count permanent weapon drops plus non-exempt power-ups (a second grant of an owned kind does not take a second slot). Weapon levels come from repeated permanent grants (`equipWeapon(id, true)`), so `player.weaponLevels` expresses "level N" as N permanent grants and scene 1's six level-2-to-5 weapons fill exactly six slots. `availableWhenSlotsFull` power-ups (e.g. `magnet`, `mineral_scoop`) remain usable for pulling the action to the ship without distorting the slot story.
- **Assumption — scene 6 is a deliberate reprise, not a duplicate.** It reuses scene 4's pressure but must differ in enemy mix and player weapons; the hermetic scene-table test asserts the difference so a copy-paste edit cannot collapse the two beats.

## Resolved decisions (producer, 2026-10-27)

1. **Scope — config + small dev-gated setup extension (Q1: B).** Extend the `setup` seam (weapon levels 2–5, `bossHitsRemaining`, forced Hull Full reward) so the described loadouts and the three on-camera endings are deterministic; dev-gated and parity-safe.
2. **Deliverable — replace `examples/scenes.json` and record once (Q2: C + record).** The excitement-curve arc becomes the shipped example config, and the item records the video once end-to-end to verify it renders (fades, pay-offs, `--json` report).
3. **Length — ~60–75 s, longer allowed if a beat needs it (Q3: A).** Baseline ≈8–10 s capture per scene with margin for the pay-offs.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (blocking) — Implementation scope.** "The scene-capture `setup` seam cannot start weapons above level 1 and cannot guarantee on-camera endings; options (a) pure config / (b) config + small dev-gated setup extension (weapon levels 2–5, start mini-boss/boss with N hits remaining) / (c) other." — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. B".** Decision: implement (b); the extension is dev-gated and lands in the shared setup applier so gym↔game parity holds.
- **Q2 (blocking) — Deliverable placement and verification.** "(a) new `examples/video-scenes.json` + hermetic validation; (b) same + also record the video once; (c) **replace** `examples/scenes.json`." — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "2. C and record".** Decision: replace `examples/scenes.json` with the arc and record the compiled video once as verification (AC3).
- **Q3 — Video length and pacing.** "(a) ~60–75 s; (b) ~90–120 s; (c) ~30–45 s." — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "3. A (though if longer is necessary to make it fit that is OK)".** Decision: target ~60–75 s; longer windows permitted where a pay-off needs them.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does the scene tooling already express this arc?" — Research: `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`/`.d.mts`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `src/core/captureDirector.ts`, `examples/scenes.json`. Result: the schema, fades and per-scene `setup` (level/waves/loadout/power-ups/seed) exist; weapon *levels*, boss starting hits and a forced Hull Full reward do not.

# Orbital Strike does nothing

## Problem statement

The **Orbital Strike** power-up is functionally wired but reads to the player as
doing nothing: it produces **no sound at all** and reuses the generic Smart Bomb
AOE ring instead of an orbital bolt, so nothing about it says "an orbital strike
just happened". Worse, in the two most common situations the bolt is **silently
consumed with zero feedback** — no VFX, no SFX, no damage.

## Users

As a **player**, I want picking up an Orbital Strike to produce an unmistakable
event — a bolt falling from the sky onto the target with its own sound — so that
I can tell the power-up is working, and so that the permanent (hold-full) reward
is worth the choice.

As a **player**, I do not want a pickup wasted silently when it is collected
while no enemy is alive; I want the strike to land on the next target (or be
clearly signalled as unused).

## Existing state (repo research)

The power-up is **not** dead code — the damage path exists and is tested. What is
missing is the *feedback layer* plus two silent-failure paths.

1. **State + decision (working).** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` sets
   `_strikePulsePending = true` for a field pickup and `_strikePermanent = true`
   + a pulse timer for a hold-full reward (`src/powerups/effects.ts:644`).
   `EffectsRegistry.updateStrike(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:1241`) returns
   `true` exactly once for a queued pickup and then once per
   `strikeInterval()` (`max(10, 30 − 2×level)` s) for the permanent reward.
2. **Shared detection (working).** `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike`
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1655`) is called from `_tickPlayer`
   (`:878`) and forwards to the `onOrbitalStrike(damage)` hook, so the game and
   every gym run one implementation.
3. **Application (working, but visually generic).**
   `CombatScene.onOrbitalStrike` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:642`) picks the
   live enemy nearest the ship, then spawns
   `spawnNovaRing(..., ORBITAL_STRIKE_RADIUS = 40, ORBITAL_STRIKE_COLOR = 0x9ffcff)`
   plus `spawnBulletImpact(...)` and applies `damageEnemyViaAoe(target, damage)`.
   That is **the same nova-ring helper and colour family as the Smart Bomb
   pulse** (`onSmartBombPulse`, `CombatScene.ts:673`) — there is no descending
   bolt, no target marker, no telegraph, no screen flash/shake. The ring lasts
   `NOVA_RING_DURATION = 0.5` s (`src/vfx/aoeEffect.ts:25`), so it is easy to miss
   entirely during play.
4. **No SFX exists.** `src/audio/effects.ts` exports **no** orbital-strike cue
   and `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (66 cues) has **no** strike entry. The
   `onOrbitalStrike` body makes no `play*` call. The unrelated Missile-Command
   **hazard** entity (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) borrows
   `playScoutAdvanceCue` (`docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md:94`), which is
   why the hazard is audible and the power-up is silent.
5. **Silent-waste path A — no target.** `onOrbitalStrike` returns early when no
   live enemy is found (`CombatScene.ts:646`), but `updateStrike` has **already**
   cleared `_strikePulsePending`. A pickup collected between waves is therefore
   consumed with literally no effect: "it does nothing at all".
6. **Silent-waste path B — no player.** `_updateOrbitalStrike` does not guard on
   a live player; `onOrbitalStrike` does. Same silent consumption.
7. **Weak readout.** The HUD shows a `strike` row **only** while the strike is
   permanent (`src/ui/HUD.ts:523`) and never shows the time to the next bolt, so
   even an armed permanent strike looks inert.
8. **Damage is often invisible.** `strikeDamage()` is `1` hit at level 1
   (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:979`), so a bolt on a multi-HP enemy removes
   one pip and on a 1-HP grunt is indistinguishable from an ordinary bullet kill.

## Desired change

Give Orbital Strike a distinct, legible identity and remove the silent failures:

- A **descending orbital bolt** (beam/column from off-screen top down to the
  target) ending in a bright impact flash — its own VFX module, not the Smart
  Bomb ring.
- A **dedicated SFX cue** played at the bolt's impact (and, optionally, at
  telegraphed launch).
- **No silent consumption**: a queued bolt with no live target (or no live
  player) must be retained and fired on the first valid frame, or clearly
  signalled as unused.
- Optional but preferred: the HUD `strike` row shows the countdown to the next
  bolt for a permanent strike.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Distinct visual identity.** A strike (field pickup or permanent pulse)
   renders a descending bolt from the top of the play area onto the target plus
   an impact flash, through a new VFX module in `src/vfx/`, and the visual is
   demonstrably distinct from the Smart Bomb pulse (different shape/composition,
   not just a recoloured `spawnNovaRing`), asserted by unit tests on the module.
2. **Dedicated audio cue.** A new `playOrbitalStrikeSound` cue exists in
   `src/audio/effects.ts`, is registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` with
   a recipe (and baked seeds if the delivery is `baked`), and is played by the
   shared strike path; `src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts` and
   `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` stay green.
3. **No silent waste.** A strike that resolves while no live enemy (or no live
   player) is present is **not** lost: the queued bolt is retained and lands on
   the first frame with a valid target, or the pickup is explicitly signalled as
   unused. A regression test drives a pickup with no live enemy and asserts the
   bolt subsequently lands on the next live enemy.
4. **Damage path unchanged.** The bolt still applies `strikeDamage()` hits to the
   nearest live enemy through `damageEnemyViaAoe`, and still depletes enemy force
   fields through the shared `takeDamage()` seam —
   `src/scenes/core/enemyForceFieldDamageSources.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` stay green.
5. **Gym↔game parity.** The VFX/SFX and the no-silent-waste behaviour live once
   in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and are consumed by `PlayScene` and
   every gym; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body
   guard) and a gym parity test in `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`
   stay green, and the strike is observable in the gym.
6. **HUD readout (preferred).** A permanent strike's HUD row shows the countdown
   to the next bolt, asserted by a HUD test — or a documented reason it was
   deliberately left out.
7. **Hazard reviewed, not regressed.** The unrelated Missile-Command
   `orbital-strike` hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`) is confirmed
   unaffected by this change; its suite (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.test.ts`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` §"Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike")
   stays green.
8. **Testing/validation.** Every acceptance criterion above is covered by an
   automated test that fails before the change and passes after it.
9. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — including code comments, the GDD §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section
   (following the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" precedent, which documents
   the aura and cue beside the mechanics), `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
   for the new cue, and any relevant README or wiki entries.
10. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory.** No divergent copy: shared behaviour in
  `src/scenes/core/` (and shared dispatchers), consumed by `PlayScene` and every
  gym scene. Any intentional divergence must be recorded in this work item and in
  a code comment.
- **Audio goes through the cue pipeline.** A cue may not be synthesised ad hoc:
  it needs a `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` entry plus a recipe under
  `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, and (for `baked` delivery) a rebuilt WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`. The contract suite asserts every `play*` export is
  manifested.
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- Cosmetic/feel work only — do **not** re-tune strike damage, interval or drop
  weight as part of this change unless a tuning defect is found (record it as
  linked follow-up work instead).
- CHANGELOG.md is excluded (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onOrbitalStrike`: replace the generic
  `spawnNovaRing` composition with the new bolt VFX and the new cue.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateOrbitalStrike`: retain/requeue a
  bolt when no target or no player is available (the no-silent-waste seam).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `updateStrike`: expose a requeue/retain path so a
  decided bolt is not lost.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.ts` — **New.** Descending bolt + impact-flash VFX,
  registered like `src/vfx/thornsAbsorb.ts` / `aoeEffect.ts`.
- `src/vfx/orbitalStrike.test.ts` — **New.** VFX composition/distinctness tests.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — **New** `playOrbitalStrikeSound` wrapper.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `audio/toneforge/recipes/` — **New** cue
  entry and recipe.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — document the new cue row.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — countdown on the permanent `strike` row (AC6).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4.3/§4.4.4 power-up section: strike
  visibility + cue paragraph.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — gym parity + observability test.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Orbital Strike" in the report means the **power-up**
  (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.strike`, display name exactly "Orbital Strike"), not the
  Missile-Command `orbital-strike` **hazard**. Rationale: the hazard already has
  a telegraph, a falling shell, a detonation burst and a borrowed cue, whereas the
  power-up has no cue at all. Recorded as Q1 below.
- **Risk — new audio asset cost.** A `baked` cue needs a ToneForge recipe plus a
  WAV rebuild; reusing an existing electric recipe (e.g. `aihell-arc-fire`) is
  the cheap alternative. Recorded as Q2 below.
- **Risk — VFX legibility vs. visual noise.** A full-height bolt on every pulse
  may fight other screen effects; cap its draw to the target column and keep the
  duration short, and validate in `GymPowerUpsCombat` with a live player.
- **Risk — retarget semantics.** Retaining a queued bolt could stack up several
  bolts during a long enemy-free gap. Cap the retained queue at one bolt (a
  permanent strike simply resumes its interval) so the behaviour stays
  predictable and testable.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Levelling, drop-weight and interval tuning, a strike
  "charging" telegraph, and multi-target strikes are all tempting; they are
  **out of scope** and should be captured as linked follow-up work items rather
  than absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** the "[no] VFX" complaint refers to the *generic, unnoticeable*
  ring rather than a rendering defect — no rendering bug was found in research.

## Related work

- **Some power-ups appear to do nothing (AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z)** — wired this
  power-up's gameplay consumers (commit `154b7adb`); AC5 covered damage only, not
  VFX/SFX.
- **Orbital Strike substrate (AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1)** — catalogue, level curves,
  effects-registry accessors and HUD readouts for the net-new power-ups.
- **Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1)** — the
  unrelated enemy hazard (`src/entities/OrbitalStrike.ts`); reviewed for
  non-regression only.
- **Orbital-Strike falling shell projectile identity (AH-0MV822GIO005B685)** —
  the hazard projectile's visual identity; a useful precedent for giving the
  power-up its own identity.
- **Create E4 Phaser gym scene (AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13)** / Phaser orbital work —
  unrelated (`orbital` formation kind, not this power-up).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 (power-up levels, Orbital Strike row) and
  the "Thorn Field visibility + recharge" paragraph in the same section — the
  documentation precedent for describing a power-up's VFX/SFX.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — the cue catalogue the new sound must
  join.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which "Orbital Strike" does this report mean: the power-up or the
  campaign hazard?**
  Options: (a) the **power-up** (`strike`, "Orbital Strike" pickup/choice
  reward); (b) the Missile-Command **hazard** (`orbital-strike` enemy entity);
  (c) both.
  **Recommended:** (a) the power-up — it has literally no SFX and only a
  borrowed generic AOE ring, which matches "no VFX or SFX".
  — **Answer: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Research evidence: the
  power-up has zero audio cues and a generic 0.5 s ring; the hazard has a
  telegraph, a falling shell, a detonation burst and the borrowed
  `playScoutAdvanceCue`. This brief is drafted for (a); if the answer is (b) or
  (c), the scope section must be revised before planning.

- **Q2 — May we add a new baked SFX cue, or must we reuse an existing one?**
  Options: (a) **new dedicated recipe** (`aihell-orbital-strike`) + baked WAV via
  `scripts/build-audio.sh`; (b) **reuse an existing electric recipe** (e.g.
  `aihell-arc-fire`) with no new asset; (c) no new audio, make the visual carry
  the identity.
  **Recommended:** (a) a new dedicated recipe — an orbital strike is a signature
  event and should not share a cue with the arc weapon.
  — **Answer: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Constraint: whichever is
  chosen, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`
  and the audio contract tests must be updated in the same change.

- **Q3 — Should the permanent strike's HUD row show a countdown to the next
  bolt?**
  Options: (a) yes, add `next in Ns`; (b) no, keep the row as-is.
  **Recommended:** (a) yes — a 10–30 s interval is otherwise invisible, and the
  HUD already renders countdowns for other timed effects.
  — **Answer: OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). AC6 is written to accept
  either outcome with a documented reason.

- **Q4 — Is it acceptable that the strike retains a queued bolt when no enemy is
  alive (rather than being wasted)?**
  **Recommended:** yes — silently losing a rare pickup is the reported bug.
  — **Answer: OPEN QUESTION**, recorded for confirmation; AC3 is written to
  accept either retention **or** explicit "unused" signalling, so implementation
  is not blocked on this.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV01ENX00055CG1** – Missile Command telegraphed orbital strike (completed)

# Test: setup field contracts and arc table (test-first)

Test-first verification slice for the scripted-video arc (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB; covers parent AC5 and the determinism half of AC4). This item writes the failing tests that specify the new scene-`setup` fields and the seven-beat example table **before** any implementation lands, so the behaviour is pinned by tests rather than by prose.

**Test-first rule:** every test in this item must be written and observed failing (for the right reason: unknown setup field / missing behaviour) before F2, F3 and F4 turn them green. Do not weaken an assertion to make it pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — New setup fields are parsed and validated.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` covers `setup.player.weaponLevels`, `setup.bossHitsRemaining` and `setup.mineralReward`: accepted shapes parse; wrong shapes raise the documented error codes; normalisation yields documented defaults; re-normalising a normalised setup is idempotent (deep-equal).
- **AC2 — Validation is target-aware.** A field is rejected on a target that cannot consume it (`unknown-setup-field` for an unknown name, `setup-not-supported`/`unsupported-setup-field`-style code for a known-but-unsupported field on that target), and `bossHitsRemaining` is accepted only on the boss-capable targets (`GymBoss`, `GymMiniBoss`). Out-of-range values (e.g. `0`, negative, non-integer, above the entity's total HP) are rejected with a documented code.
- **AC3 — Applier behaviour is specified.** `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` asserts with a fake player that `player.weaponLevels: { rapid: 3 }` produces three permanent `equipWeapon('rapid', true)` calls (level N == N permanent grants), that `player.weapons` still grants level 1, and that a forced `mineralReward` selects the named reward instead of a random one.
- **AC4 — Boss hit preview is specified.** A test asserts that `bossHitsRemaining` reaches the spawned boss/mini-boss as `initialHp` (spawn-path unit test against `GymBoss`/`GymMiniBoss` seams), and that an absent field leaves today's full-HP spawn unchanged.
- **AC5 — The seven-beat arc table is pinned.** `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (or a dedicated `examples/scenes.json` table test) asserts the exact seven entries: beat order, `target`, `playMs`/`captureMs` window presence, `label`, per-scene seed, `player.weaponLevels`/`player.weapons` and slot counts, `bossHitsRemaining` on the mini-boss and boss beats, and `mineralReward` on the humble-origins beat. Scene 6 (reprise) is asserted to differ from scene 4 in both enemy mix and player weapons, so a copy-paste edit cannot collapse the two beats.
- **AC6 — Doc parity is specified.** `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` asserts `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents each new setup field (two-way parity with the parser's field list) and each new error code, and that the shipped example parses. (The doc additions themselves land in F5.)
- **AC7 — No test is vacuous.** Every new test asserts observable behaviour (returned value, thrown code, or call list); no test merely asserts a constant equals itself.

- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — applier tests for weapon levels and forced reward.

## Plan traceability

- **Parent AC5 — testing and validation.** Hermetic tests extending `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` cover parse, validate, normalise and idempotence of the new setup fields, the exact scene-table assertions for the seven beats (targets, loadouts, slot counts, `bossHitsRemaining`, `mineralReward`, seeds), applier tests in `sceneSetup.test.ts` for weapon levels and the forced reward, and updated `examples/scenes.json` pins in `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` and `capture-scenes.test.ts`. # Setup seam: weapon levels and forced mineral reward

Dev-gated extension of the shared scene-`setup` seam (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, parent AC2 parts (a) and (c), plus AC4 for seed/level determinism). Makes weapon levels 2-5 and the Hull Full pay-off expressible in a capture config **without** any shipped-game behaviour change.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can write `"player": { "weaponLevels": { "rapid": 4 } }` in a scene config and get a scene that starts with a level-4 rapid, and I can force the full-hold resolution to the Hull Full reward so the pay-off lands on camera deterministically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — `player.weaponLevels` is a first-class setup field.** Validated and normalised in the pure `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` module (per-weapon integer levels within the documented range 1-5 for capture use), typed in `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts`, and accepted on every setup-capable target that already consumes `setup.player` (or documented as restricted, if restricted). Unknown weapon ids raise the existing `unknown-weapon-id` code; invalid levels raise a documented code.
- **AC2 — The applier implements weapon levels through the existing seam.** `applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants `weaponLevels[id] = N` as N permanent `equipWeapon(id, true)` calls, and `SceneSetupState` gains the typed field. `player.weapons` keeps its level-1 semantics unchanged. A scene without the field is byte-for-byte behaviour-compatible with today.
- **AC3 — `setup.mineralReward` forces the hold-full resolution.** `SceneSetupState` and the parser carry an optional reward id; `GymLevel._resolveMineralHold` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`) resolves to that reward when configured (through the shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`) and falls back to today's `randomChoiceStrategy` when absent. An unknown/unavailable reward id is rejected at parse time rather than silently ignored.
- **AC4 — Dev-gating holds.** `npm run check-bundle` stays green (no new production surface) and `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green (the change configures existing state through the shared applier; no divergent gameplay copy).
- **AC5 — Tests from F1 turn green.** The relevant assertions in `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` and `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` pass; failures are fixed in code, not by relaxing the tests (any genuine spec change is recorded as a comment on both items).
- **AC6 — Error codes are documented in the module.** Each new code is added to `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES` with a doc comment, and is listed in `SCENE_SETUP_COMMON_FIELDS`/target-extra-fields as appropriate so the docs parity test can see it.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — validation/normalisation/error codes/field lists.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` — `SceneSetupPlayer.weaponLevels`, `SceneSetup.mineralReward` declarations.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — `SceneSetupState` + `applySceneSetup` weapon-level grants + reward selection seam.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — `_resolveMineralHold` honouring the forced reward.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — tests from F1.

## Dependencies

Blocked by F1 (test-first contracts).


## Plan traceability

- **Parent AC2 — deterministic arc beats via a small dev-gated setup extension.** The scene `setup` seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` to gyms) gains, with validated and normalised support in `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` plus `.d.mts` types and error codes: `player.weaponLevels` (per-weapon permanent levels 2-5), `setup.bossHitsRemaining` (the boss gyms `GymBoss` and `GymMiniBoss` spawn their entity with that many hits left) and `setup.mineralReward` (the hold-full choice in the level gyms resolves to that reward id). Each new field is validated, normalised and documented alongside the existing ones; the extension is dev-gated and inert for production, `npm run check-bundle` and the gym-game parity suite stay green, and no shipped-game gameplay behaviour changes.

# Boss gyms honour bossHitsRemaining

Dev-gated extension that lets a scene config start the mini-boss/boss close to death so its death lands inside the capture window (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, parent AC2 part (b)). Reuses the existing `initialHp` constructor seam already used by `PlayScene.startDevBossScenario(bossHitsRemaining)` — no new gameplay behaviour.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I set `"setup": { "bossHitsRemaining": 6 }` on a `GymBoss`/`GymMiniBoss` scene and the entity spawns with 6 hits left, so the auto-firing ship finishes it on camera within the scene window.

## Acceptance Criteria

Supplying it to any other target is rejected, not ignored.
- **AC2 — The boss gyms consume the field.** `GymBoss` and `GymMiniBoss` pass `initialHp` into their entity spawn path (`Boss`/`MiniBoss` already accept `initialHp`; the spawn goes through `GymFormationScene`'s shared `createEntity`/`_spawnFormation` config), so the spawned entity starts with that many hits in its current phase while keeping the existing total-phase structure.

  1. **Opening spectacle** — many enemies, lots of minerals/upgrades, all six upgrade slots filled with weapons at levels 2-5.

# Test: cross-scene spawn/fire/march parity for the level-launch path (red-before)

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC1, AC2, AC3). **Test-first item — create and land the failing tests before any production change.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want a cross-scene equivalence test that boots `PlayScene` and the
level-launch gym (`GymLevel`, and `GymBotTuning` through inheritance) with the *same* seeded wave
and asserts identical spawn transit, identical fire cadence and identical march motion, so a
future divergence in the spawn seam cannot land without the suite failing.

## Problem

Parity coverage today exists for `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and
`GymFodderEnemies` (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for the
level-launch path. `GymLevel.test.ts` even works around the missing `shootEnabled` hand-off by
setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand, which is itself part of the defect.

## Required behaviour (the assertions that must exist)

1. **Orbital transit destination (AC1).** For an orbital wave (the Phaser), every frame of the
   wormhole spawn window in `GymLevel` must resolve a destination equal to the entity's live
   `formationSlot()` — asserted frame by frame against the same wave driven through `PlayScene`.
   No frame may place the Phaser on the straight grid line `startX + driftX + col*spacingX`, and
   the landing position at the end of the window must equal the orbital slot (no snap).
2. **Fire cadence (AC2).** A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` must produce the same number
   of bullets, at the same `scene.time.now` ticks, with the same bullet speed, in `GymLevel` /
   `GymBotTuning` as in `PlayScene`. The test must **not** set `shootEnabled` by hand — it must
   flow from the wave definition (`src/waves/Formations.ts`, campaign levels 4+).
3. **March block (AC3).** For a `march` wave, stepping through an identical `dt` sequence must
   produce the same base position (x, y, direction) and the same per-member offsets in `GymLevel`
   as `PlayScene`'s `marchState` block, including at least one edge reversal and one drop.

## Implementation guidance

- Put the new coverage in `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` (already the level-gym parity home,
  AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) unless the file becomes unwieldy, in which case add
  `src/scenes/gym/spawnParity.test.ts` and keep the level-parity file for scaling/cadence.
- Reuse the existing `bootScene` harness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) and the existing cross-scene
  equivalence patterns in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — do not invent a second harness.
- Express the wave with a fixed seed so both scenes see identical content (the `sceneSetup` seed
  seam, `resolveSetupSeed`). No `Math.random`.
- Mark the new assertions with Vitest `it.fails(...)` (the repo's red-before/green-after
  convention, cf. `levelParity.test.ts` header) **or** `it(...)` with an explicit
  `// red-before: fails until AH-<child-of-this-item> lands` note, and flip them to `it` in the
  fix item. Whichever convention the surrounding file already uses must be followed.
- The flip-to-green work belongs to the implementation children (shared seam
  AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN, then the `GymLevel` parity fix AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B). This item is complete
  as soon as the tests exist and demonstrably fail on the pre-fix HEAD; the red-before markers are
  flipped by AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B.

## Red-before evidence

Record in a comment: the exact failing assertion output on pre-fix HEAD (all three assertions),
plus the commit hash of the test-only commit. This is the reproducibility proof the parent ACs
require.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A cross-scene test asserts, frame by frame, that `GymLevel`'s orbital spawn
  destination equals the live `formationSlot()` for every frame of the spawn window, and that the
  end-of-window position equals the orbital slot; it fails on pre-fix HEAD and the failure output
  is recorded on this item.
- [ ] AC2 — A cross-scene test asserts identical post-spawn fire cadence, bullet count and bullet
  speed for a wave with `shootEnabled: true` in `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` vs `PlayScene`, without
  any hand-set `shootEnabled`; it fails on pre-fix HEAD (zero bullets in the gym) and the output is
  recorded.
- [ ] AC3 — A cross-scene test drives an identical `dt` sequence through a `march` wave and
  asserts identical base position, direction and member offsets in the gym vs `PlayScene`,
  including one edge reversal and one drop; it fails on pre-fix HEAD and the output is recorded.
- [ ] AC4 — `GymBotTuning` is covered by inheritance or an explicit assertion (the reported
  symptom was observed in `GymBotTuning`, which extends `GymLevel`).
- [ ] AC5 — No production file is modified by this item (tests and test helpers only), and the
  pre-existing suite stays green apart from the new red-before assertions.

## Key files

- `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` (extend, or new sibling `spawnParity.test.ts`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` (the hand-set `shootEnabled` workaround at ~:599 is the
  evidence to replace)
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` (reuse `bootScene`)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` (campaign waves with `shootEnabled` and `march` groups)

## Constraints

- Test-only slice: no behaviour change, no refactor.
- No fixed sleeps for the spawn window — drive the clock explicitly.

## Parent AC coverage (traceability)

This child contributes to parent AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV. This item establishes the red-before cross-scene evidence; the sibling fix items flip it green.

Parent acceptance criteria satisfied (restated verbatim from the parent brief):

- **Parent AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).**

- **Parent AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.**

- **Parent AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.**
